status_paragraphs.name: GrantTraversal
paragraph: **STATUS: OPEN.** In the first-read `souji-seat-audit.py`, `run()` takes `spec["reportDir"]` with only `.rstrip("/")`, concatenates it to `lane` to form each seat's `report`, and supplies that path to `audit_seat()` as an allowed target. `target_verdict()` rejects `..` components in the *transcript target*, but for absolute targets it then compares `_norm(target)` against `_norm(p)` for every allowed path. Thus traversal in the authority-side report directory is collapsed into a grant before the lane boundary is checked. The per-item `OWN ONLY` extractor similarly accepts an absolute string without rejecting `..` (`owned_paths()`); it can reach the same normalized-allow path.

status_paragraphs.name: ReceiptAuditor
paragraph: **MEDIUM — C1 receipt can fingerprint disk bytes other than the executing auditor module.** `tools/souji-seat-audit.py:364-365` reads `Path(__file__)` from disk only after `run()` has been entered; the module is already loaded before the CLI calls `run()` at lines 612-626. The drift check at lines 401-404 compares the file only with the bytes captured at line 364, and lines 410-415 publish that snapshot as the auditor input digest. **STATUS: OPEN** — [INFERENCE] If an already-imported auditor's source path is replaced before `run()` captures it (or a concurrent edit lands in the CLI load-to-capture window), the old loaded code can execute while the new stable file's digest is returned; the late reread passes. This does not establish a fresh runtime occurrence, but it is a falsifiable gap in binding the receipt to the auditor that actually ran.

status_paragraphs.name: InputR13Fixtures
paragraph: **STATUS: OPEN.** `tools/souji-rev-pin.py:156-164` walks selected directories with `os.walk(..., followlinks=False)` but supplies no `onerror` handler. Python documents that `os.walk` ignores `scandir()` errors by default ([Python `os.walk` docs, lines 3703-3735](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.walk)). If an unreadable nested directory contains a new untracked regular leaf, traversal can silently omit it; because the leaf is absent from both the Git tree’s expected mapping and the incomplete actual mapping, `input_snapshot` can return equality instead of refusal. This breaks the required exact added-leaf check and can let the r13 runner reach its record write with an incomplete snapshot. This is a source-derived counterexample, **not executed**.
status_paragraphs.disposition: open; source/limit retained pending pinned runtime and independent closure

status_paragraphs.name: InputR14Frozen
paragraph: **STATUS: OPEN** — The preregistered C2 oracle requires every actual caller to reject a dirty helper with exit 2 and no output. A syntactically invalid dirty helper instead escapes as an uncaught `SyntaxError`, so these callers do not meet the specified refusal contract. In `census/round-14/run-verification.py:54-57`, the revision helper is loaded with `exec_module()` before the `try` that begins at line 60; its `__main__` handler at lines 167-172 catches only `OSError`, `ValueError`, and `RuntimeError`, not `SyntaxError`. The targeted wrapper likewise excludes `SyntaxError` in its handler (`census/round-14/run-targeted.py:62-67`); its top-level r14-runner import is also unguarded (`:16-18`). The cache demonstration loads the helper before its `Refusal` handler (`census/round-14/cache-demonstration.py:194-200`), and invokes this check at `:1137` before its later protected block (`:1150`); its entry point has no conversion of that loader error to exit 2. Thus a simple counterexample is a dirty helper containing invalid Python: loading aborts before the byte comparison, producing Python's uncaught-error exit rather than the required controlled exit 2. No evidence here claims this case was executed.
status_paragraphs.disposition: open; source/limit retained pending pinned runtime and independent closure
